<h1 id="figma-api">Figma API v0.46.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

This is the OpenAPI specification for the [Figma REST API](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/).

Note: we are releasing the OpenAPI specification as a beta given the large surface area and complexity of the REST API. If you notice any inaccuracies with the specification, please [file an issue](https://github.com/figma/rest-api-spec/issues).

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.figma.com">https://api.figma.com</a>

<a href="https://www.figma.com/developer-terms/">Terms of service</a>
Email: <a href="mailto:support@figma.com">support@figma.com</a> 

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/">Figma REST API Documentation</a>

# Authentication

* API Key (PersonalAccessToken)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Figma-Token**, in: header.

* API Key (PlanAccessToken)
    - Parameter Name: **X-Figma-Token**, in: header.

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://www.figma.com/oauth](https://www.figma.com/oauth)
    - Token URL = [https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token](https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token)
    - Refresh URL = [https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh](https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|current_user:read|Read your name, email, and profile image.|
|file_comments:read|Read the comments for files.|
|file_comments:write|Post and delete comments and comment reactions in files.|
|file_content:read|Read the contents of files, such as nodes and the editor type.|
|file_duplicate:write|Duplicate files into folders. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.|
|file_dev_resources:read|Read dev resources in files.|
|file_dev_resources:write|Write to dev resources in files.|
|file_metadata:read|Read metadata of files.|
|file_variables:read|Read variables in Figma file. Note: this is only available to members in Enterprise organizations.|
|file_variables:write|Write to variables in Figma file. Note: this is only available to members in Enterprise organizations.|
|file_versions:read|Read the version history for files you can access.|
|files:read|Deprecated. Read files, projects, users, versions, comments, components & styles, and webhooks.|
|library_analytics:read|Read library analytics data.|
|library_assets:read|Read data of individual published components and styles.|
|library_content:read|Read published components and styles of files.|
|project_metadata:read|Read metadata of projects.|
|projects:read|List projects and files in projects.|
|folder_metadata:read|Read metadata of folders.|
|folders:read|List folders and files in folders.|
|folders:write|Create folders. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.|
|team_library_content:read|Read published components and styles of teams.|
|team_members:write|Invite members to teams. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.|
|teams:read|Read team metadata. Available to private OAuth apps in Professional, Organization, and Enterprise plans, and to plan access tokens in Organization and Enterprise plans.|
|teams:write|Create teams. Available only to private OAuth apps in an Enterprise plan.|
|webhooks:read|Read metadata of webhooks.|
|webhooks:write|Create and manage webhooks.|

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://www.figma.com/oauth](https://www.figma.com/oauth)
    - Token URL = [https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token](https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/token)
    - Refresh URL = [https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh](https://api.figma.com/v1/oauth/refresh)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|org:activity_log_read|Read activity logs in the organization.|

<h1 id="figma-api-files">Files</h1>

Get file JSON, images, and other file-related content.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/file-endpoints/">File endpoints documentation</a>

## Get file JSON

<a id="opIdgetFile"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}`

Returns the document identified by `file_key` as a JSON object. The file key can be parsed from any Figma file url: `https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/{title}`.

The `document` property contains a node of type `DOCUMENT`.

The `components` property contains a mapping from node IDs to component metadata. This is to help you determine which components each instance comes from.

<h3 id="get-file-json-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to export JSON from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|
|version|query|string|false|A specific version ID to get. Omitting this will get the current version of the file.|
|ids|query|string|false|Comma separated list of nodes that you care about in the document. If specified, only a subset of the document will be returned corresponding to the nodes listed, their children, and everything between the root node and the listed nodes.<br><br>Note: There may be other nodes included in the returned JSON that are outside the ancestor chains of the desired nodes. The response may also include dependencies of anything in the nodes' subtrees. For example, if a node subtree contains an instance of a local component that lives elsewhere in that file, that component and its ancestor chain will also be included.<br><br>For historical reasons, top-level canvas nodes are always returned, regardless of whether they are listed in the `ids` parameter. This quirk may be removed in a future version of the API.|
|depth|query|number|false|Positive integer representing how deep into the document tree to traverse. For example, setting this to 1 returns only Pages, setting it to 2 returns Pages and all top level objects on each page. Not setting this parameter returns all nodes.|
|geometry|query|string|false|Set to "paths" to export vector data.|
|plugin_data|query|string|false|A comma separated list of plugin IDs and/or the string "shared". Any data present in the document written by those plugins will be included in the result in the `pluginData` and `sharedPluginData` properties.|
|branch_data|query|boolean|false|Returns branch metadata for the requested file. If the file is a branch, the main file's key will be included in the returned response. If the file has branches, their metadata will be included in the returned response. Default: false.|

<h3 id="get-file-json-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response from the GET /v1/files/{file_key} endpoint.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. Parameters are invalid or malformed. Please check the input formats. This error can also happen if the requested resources are too large to complete the request, which results in a timeout. Please reduce the number and size of objects requested.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|The request was valid, but the server is refusing action. The user might not have the necessary permissions for a resource, or may need an account of some sort.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The requested file or resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|In some cases API requests may be throttled or rate limited. Please wait a while before attempting the request again (typically a minute).|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|An internal server error occurred.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-file-json-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|true|none|The name of the file as it appears in the editor.|
|role|[Role](#schemarole)|true|none|The role of the user making the API request in relation to the file.|
|lastModified|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 time at which the file was last modified.|
|editorType|string|true|none|The type of editor associated with this file.|
|thumbnailUrl|string|false|none|A URL to a thumbnail image of the file.|
|version|string|true|none|The version number of the file. This number is incremented when a file is modified and can be used to check if the file has changed between requests.|
|document|[DocumentNode](#schemadocumentnode)|true|none|none|
|components|object|true|none|A mapping from component IDs to component metadata.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[Component](#schemacomponent)|false|none|A description of a main component. Helps you identify which component instances are attached to.|
|componentSets|object|true|none|A mapping from component set IDs to component set metadata.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[ComponentSet](#schemacomponentset)|false|none|A description of a component set, which is a node containing a set of variants of a component.|
|schemaVersion|number|true|none|The version of the file schema that this file uses.|
|styles|object|true|none|A mapping from style IDs to style metadata.|
|» **additionalProperties**|[Style](#schemastyle)|false|none|A set of properties that can be applied to nodes and published. Styles for a property can be created in the corresponding property's panel while editing a file.|
|linkAccess|string|false|none|The share permission level of the file link.|
|mainFileKey|string|false|none|The key of the main file for this file. If present, this file is a component or component set.|
|branches|[object]|false|none|A list of branches for this file.|
|» key|string|true|none|The key of the branch.|
|» name|string|true|none|The name of the branch.|
|» thumbnail_url|string|true|none|A URL to a thumbnail image of the branch.|
|» last_modified|string(date-time)|true|none|The UTC ISO 8601 time at which the branch was last modified.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|role|owner|
|role|editor|
|role|viewer|
|editorType|figma|
|editorType|figjam|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
PersonalAccessToken, PlanAccessToken, OAuth2 ( Scopes: file_content:read files:read )
</aside>

## Get file JSON for specific nodes

<a id="opIdgetFileNodes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/nodes?ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}/nodes`

Returns the nodes referenced to by `ids` as a JSON object. The nodes are retrieved from the Figma file referenced to by `file_key`.

The node ID and file key can be parsed from any Figma node url: `https://www.figma.com/file/{file_key}/{title}?node-id={id}`

The `name`, `lastModified`, `thumbnailUrl`, `editorType`, and `version` attributes are all metadata of the specified file.

The `linkAccess` field describes the file link share permission level. There are 5 types of permissions a shared link can have: `"inherit"`, `"view"`, `"edit"`, `"org_view"`, and `"org_edit"`. `"inherit"` is the default permission applied to files created in a team project, and will inherit the project's permissions. `"org_view"` and `"org_edit"` restrict the link to org users.

The `document` attribute contains a Node of type `DOCUMENT`.

The `components` key contains a mapping from node IDs to component metadata. This is to help you determine which components each instance comes from.

By default, no vector data is returned. To return vector data, pass the geometry=paths parameter to the endpoint.
Each node can also inherit properties from applicable styles. The styles key contains a mapping from style IDs to style metadata.

Important: the nodes map may contain values that are `null`. This may be due to the node id not existing within the specified file.

<h3 id="get-file-json-for-specific-nodes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to export JSON from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|
|ids|query|string|true|A comma separated list of node IDs to retrieve and convert.|
|version|query|string|false|A specific version ID to get. Omitting this will get the current version of the file.|
|depth|query|number|false|Positive integer representing how deep into the node tree to traverse. For example, setting this to 1 will return only the children directly underneath the desired nodes. Not setting this parameter returns all nodes.<br><br>Note: this parameter behaves differently from the same parameter in the `GET /v1/files/:key` endpoint. In this endpoint, the depth will be counted starting from the desired node rather than the document root node.|
|geometry|query|string|false|Set to "paths" to export vector data.|
|plugin_data|query|string|false|A comma separated list of plugin IDs and/or the string "shared". Any data present in the document written by those plugins will be included in the result in the `pluginData` and `sharedPluginData` properties.|

## Render images of file nodes

<a id="opIdgetImages"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/images/string?ids=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/images/{file_key}`

Renders images from a file.

If no error occurs, `"images"` will be populated with a map from node IDs to URLs of the rendered images, and `"status"` will be omitted. The image assets will expire after 30 days. Images up to 32 megapixels can be exported. Any images that are larger will be scaled down.

Important: the image map may contain values that are `null`. This indicates that rendering of that specific node has failed. This may be due to the node id not existing, or other reasons such has the node having no renderable components. It is guaranteed that any node that was requested for rendering will be represented in this map whether or not the render succeeded.

To render multiple images from the same file, use the `ids` query parameter to specify multiple node ids.

```
GET /v1/images/:key?ids=1:2,1:3,1:4
```


<h3 id="render-images-of-file-nodes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to export images from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|
|ids|query|string|true|A comma separated list of node IDs to render.|
|version|query|string|false|A specific version ID to get. Omitting this will get the current version of the file.|
|scale|query|number|false|A number between 0.01 and 4, the image scaling factor.|
|format|query|string|false|A string enum for the image output format.|
|svg_outline_text|query|boolean|false|Whether text elements are rendered as outlines (vector paths) or as `<text>` elements in SVGs.<br><br>Rendering text elements as outlines guarantees that the text looks exactly the same in the SVG as it does in the browser/inside Figma.<br><br>Exporting as `<text>` allows text to be selectable inside SVGs and generally makes the SVG easier to read. However, this relies on the browser's rendering engine which can vary between browsers and/or operating systems. As such, visual accuracy is not guaranteed as the result could look different than in Figma.|
|svg_include_id|query|boolean|false|Whether to include id attributes for all SVG elements. Adds the layer name to the `id` attribute of an svg element.|
|svg_include_node_id|query|boolean|false|Whether to include node id attributes for all SVG elements. Adds the node id to a `data-node-id` attribute of an svg element.|
|svg_simplify_stroke|query|boolean|false|Whether to simplify inside/outside strokes and use stroke attribute if possible instead of `<mask>`.|
|contents_only|query|boolean|false|Whether content that overlaps the node should be excluded from rendering. Passing false (i.e., rendering overlaps) may increase processing time, since more of the document must be included in rendering.|
|use_absolute_bounds|query|boolean|false|Use the full dimensions of the node regardless of whether or not it is cropped or the space around it is empty. Use this to export text nodes without cropping.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|format|jpg|
|format|png|
|format|svg|
|format|pdf|

```json
  }
}
```

## Get image fills

<a id="opIdgetImageFills"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/images \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}/images`

Returns download links for all images present in image fills in a document. Image fills are how Figma represents any user supplied images. When you drag an image into Figma, we create a rectangle with a single fill that represents the image, and the user is able to transform the rectangle (and properties on the fill) as they wish.

This endpoint returns a mapping from image references to the URLs at which the images may be download. Image URLs will expire after no more than 14 days. Image references are located in the output of the GET files endpoint under the `imageRef` attribute in a `Paint`.

<h3 id="get-image-fills-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to get image URLs from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "error": false,
  "status": 200,
  "meta": {
    "images": {
      "property1": "http://example.com",
      "property2": "http://example.com"
    }
  }
}
```

## Duplicate a file

<a id="opIdpostFileDuplicate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/duplicate \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/files/{file_key}/duplicate`

Duplicates a main file or branch into the specified folder as a new standalone file. The source file and destination folder must belong to the Enterprise plan associated with the private OAuth app. The authenticated user must be able to export the source file, edit the destination folder, and create files of the source editor type.

The copy uses the source's latest saved checkpoint and may not include recent unsaved changes. This endpoint is available only to Enterprise plans.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder_id": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="duplicate-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|The key of the main file or branch to duplicate.|
|body|body|object|true|The destination for the duplicated file.|
|» folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to create the duplicated file in.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "file_key": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "folder_id": "string",
  "editor_type": "figma",
  "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

```json
  "error": true,

}
```

```json
}
```

```json
}
```

```json
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

## Get versions of a file

<a id="opIdgetFileVersions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}/versions`

This endpoint fetches the version history of a file, allowing you to see the progression of a file over time. You can then use this information to render a specific version of the file, via another endpoint.

<h3 id="get-versions-of-a-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to get version history from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|
|page_size|query|number|false|The number of items returned in a page of the response. If not included, `page_size` is `30`.|
|before|query|number|false|A version ID for one of the versions in the history. Gets versions before this ID. Used for paginating. If the response is not paginated, this link returns the same data in the current response.|
|after|query|number|false|A version ID for one of the versions in the history. Gets versions after this ID. Used for paginating. If the response is not paginated, this property is not included.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "versions": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "label": "string",
      "description": "string",
      "user": {
        "id": "string",
        "handle": "string",
        "img_url": "string"
      },
      "thumbnail_url": "string"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "prev_page": "string",
    "next_page": "string"
  }
}
```

```json
  "status": 403,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
}
```

## Add a comment to a file

<a id="opIdpostComment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/comments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "message": "string",
    "comment_id": "string",
    "client_meta": {
      "x": 0,
      "y": 0
    }
  }'
```

`POST /v1/files/{file_key}/comments`

Posts a new comment on the file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "message": "string",
  "comment_id": "string",
  "client_meta": {
    "x": 0,
    "y": 0
  }
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|» » *oneOf*|body|[Region](#schemaregion)|false|Position of a region comment on the canvas.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[FrameOffsetRegion](#schemaframeoffsetregion)|false|Position of a region comment relative to the frame to which it is attached.|

## Add a reaction to a comment

<a id="opIdpostCommentReaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/comments/string/reactions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "emoji": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/files/{file_key}/comments/{comment_id}/reactions`

Posts a new comment reaction on a file comment.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emoji": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-reaction-to-a-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to post comment reactions to. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|
|comment_id|path|string|true|ID of comment to react to.|
|body|body|object|true|Reaction to post.|
|» emoji|body|[Emoji](#schemaemoji)|true|The emoji type of reaction as shortcode (e.g. `:heart:`, `:+1::skin-tone-2:`). The list of accepted emoji shortcodes can be found in [this file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/missive/emoji-mart/main/packages/emoji-mart-data/sets/14/native.json) under the top-level emojis and aliases fields, with optional skin tone modifiers when applicable.|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "error": false
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
}
```

## Delete a reaction

<a id="opIddeleteCommentReaction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/comments/string/reactions?emoji=string' \
```

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

Deprecated in favor of [Get top-level folders in a team](https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/folders-endpoints/). You can use this endpoint to get a list of the top-level Projects (now called "folders") within the specified team. This will only return projects visible to the authenticated user or owner of the developer token. Note: it is not currently possible to programmatically obtain the team id of a user just from a token. To obtain a team id, navigate to a team page of a team you are a part of. The team id will be present in the URL after the word team and before your team name.

## Create a team

<a id="opIdpostTeam"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/teams \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "description": "string",
    "sharing_audience_control": "org_view",
    "org_discoverability": "hidden",
    "workspace_id": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/teams`

Creates a team in the Enterprise plan associated with a private OAuth app. The app uses the authenticated user's permissions, and that user becomes the team owner. The request is subject to the same team-creation controls and permissions as team creation in Figma.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "sharing_audience_control": "org_view",
  "org_discoverability": "hidden",
  "workspace_id": "string"
}
```

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateTeamRequest](#schemacreateteamrequest)|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the team.|
|» description|body|string \| null|false|A description of the team.|
|» sharing_audience_control|body|string|true|The audience that can discover and join the team. Workspace audiences require a workspace_id.|
|» org_discoverability|body|string \| null|false|Whether organization members can discover an invite-only team. Required for invite_only and not accepted for other audiences.|
|» workspace_id|body|string \| null|false|The workspace in which to create the team. Required for workspace audiences.|

## Invite users to a team

<a id="opIdpostTeamInvites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/teams/string/invites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "emails": [
      "user@example.com"
    ],
    "role": "viewer"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites`

Invites users to a team with the requested role. This endpoint is available only to private OAuth apps associated with an Enterprise plan, and the team must belong to that plan. The authenticated user must be allowed to grant the requested role on the team.

Each email address is processed independently. Per-address failures are returned in `errors` with HTTP 200, even if `invites` is empty. Always check `errors` to determine which addresses could not be invited.

Existing team members keep their current role when it is higher than the requested role.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "emails": [
    "user@example.com"
  ],
  "role": "viewer"
}
```

<h3 id="invite-users-to-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|string|true|The ID of the team to invite users to.|
|body|body|[InviteTeamMembersRequest](#schemainviteteammembersrequest)|true|The users to invite and the team role to grant them.|
|» emails|body|[string(email)]|true|The email addresses to invite.|
|» role|body|string|true|The role to grant each invited member. Existing roles are never downgraded.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|viewer|
|» role|editor|
|» role|admin|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "invites": [
    {
      "email": "alex@example.com",
      "role": "editor"
    }
  ],
  "errors": [
    {
      "email": "sam@example.com",
      "error": "Unable to invite this email address."
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": true,
  "status": 400,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 401 Response

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "status": 0,
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="invite-users-to-a-team-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. Per-address failures return HTTP 200. Always inspect `errors`; `invites` may be empty.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. The response may be JSON or HTML.|Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Error response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. The error payload depends on where the request failed.|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Error response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. The error payload depends on where the request failed.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Error response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. The error payload depends on where the request failed.|Inline|
|413|Payload Too Large|Request body too large.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|Error response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. The error payload depends on where the request failed.|Inline|
|500|Internal Server Error|Error response from the POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/invites endpoint. The error payload depends on where the request failed.|Inline|

<h1 id="figma-api-folders">Folders</h1>

## Create a folder

<a id="opIdpostTeamFolder"></a>

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/teams/string/folders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \

    "name": "string",
    "sharing_audience_control": "plan_view"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/teams/{team_id}/folders`

## Get top-level folders in a team

<a id="opIdgetTeamFolders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v2/teams/string/folders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/teams/{team_id}/folders`

Get a list of the top-level folders (previously called "projects") within the specified team. Subfolders can be traversed with the GET /v2/folders/{folder_id}/folders endpoint. It is not possible to programmatically obtain team IDs. To obtain a team ID, navigate to the team page in the Figma file browser. The team ID is present in the URL after the word team. For example, in `https://www.figma.com/files/181033233908053158/team/1535685101263221741`, the team ID is `1535685101263221741`.

<h3 id="get-top-level-folders-in-a-team-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|string|true|ID of the team to list folders from|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "folders": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "parent_folder_id": "string",
      "sharing_audience_control": "plan_view",
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "error": true,

}
```

```json
}
```

## Get team components

<a id="opIdgetTeamComponents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/teams/string/components \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/components`

Get a paginated list of published components within a team library.

<h3 id="get-team-components-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|string|true|Id of the team to list components from.|
|page_size|query|number|false|Number of items to return in a paged list of results. Defaults to 30. Maximum of 1000.|
|after|query|number|false|Cursor indicating which id after which to start retrieving components for. Exclusive with before. The cursor value is an internally tracked integer that doesn't correspond to any Ids.|
|before|query|number|false|Cursor indicating which id before which to start retrieving components for. Exclusive with after. The cursor value is an internally tracked integer that doesn't correspond to any Ids.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "error": false,
  "meta": {
    "components": [
      {
        "key": "string",
        "file_key": "string",
        "node_id": "string",
        "thumbnail_url": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "description": "string",
        "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "user": {
          "id": "string",
          "handle": "string",
          "img_url": "string"
        },
        "containing_frame": {
          "nodeId": "string",
          "name": "string",
          "backgroundColor": "string",
          "pageId": "string",
          "pageName": "string",
          "containingStateGroup": {
            "nodeId": "string",
            "name": "string"
          },
          "containingComponentSet": {
            "nodeId": "string",
            "name": "string"
          }
        }
      }
    ],
    "cursor": {
      "before": 0,
      "after": 0
    }
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "status": 400,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "status": 403,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
```

## Get team component sets

<a id="opIdgetTeamComponentSets"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/teams/string/component_sets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/teams/{team_id}/component_sets`

Get a paginated list of published component sets within a team library.

<h3 id="get-team-component-sets-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|team_id|path|string|true|Id of the team to list component sets from.|
|page_size|query|number|false|Number of items to return in a paged list of results. Defaults to 30.|
|after|query|number|false|Cursor indicating which id after which to start retrieving component sets for. Exclusive with before. The cursor value is an internally tracked integer that doesn't correspond to any Ids.|
|before|query|number|false|Cursor indicating which id before which to start retrieving component sets for. Exclusive with after. The cursor value is an internally tracked integer that doesn't correspond to any Ids.|

<h1 id="figma-api-webhooks">Webhooks</h1>

Interact with team webhooks as a team admin.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/webhooks-endpoints/">Webhook endpoints documentation</a>

## Get webhooks by context or plan

<a id="opIdgetWebhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v2/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v2/webhooks`

Returns a list of webhooks corresponding to the context or plan provided, if they exist. For plan, the webhooks for all contexts that you have access to will be returned, and theresponse is paginated

<h3 id="get-webhooks-by-context-or-plan-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|context|query|string|false|Context to create the resource on. Should be "team", "project", or "file".|
|context_id|query|string|false|The id of the context that you want to get attached webhooks for. If you're using context_id, you cannot use plan_api_id.|
|plan_api_id|query|string|false|The id of your plan. Use this to get all webhooks for all contexts you have access to. If you're using plan_api_id, you cannot use context or context_id. When you use plan_api_id, the response is paginated.|
|cursor|query|string|false|If you're using plan_api_id, this is the cursor to use for pagination. If you're using context or context_id, this parameter is ignored. Provide the next_page or prev_page value from the previous response to get the next or previous page of results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "event_type": "PING",
      "team_id": "string",
      "context": "string",
      "context_id": "string",
      "plan_api_id": "string",
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "client_id": "string",
      "passcode": "string",
      "endpoint": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "prev_page": "string",
    "next_page": "string"
  }
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": true,
  "status": 400,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
  "status": 403,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v2/webhooks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "event_type": "PING",
    "team_id": "string",
    "context": "string",
    "context_id": "string",
    "endpoint": "string",
    "passcode": "string",
    "status": "ACTIVE",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v2/webhooks`

Create a new webhook which will call the specified endpoint when the event triggers. By default, this webhook will automatically send a PING event to the endpoint when it is created. If this behavior is not desired, you can create the webhook and set the status to PAUSED and reactivate it later.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_type": "PING",
  "team_id": "string",
  "context": "string",
  "context_id": "string",
  "endpoint": "string",
  "passcode": "string",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-webhook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|The webhook to create.|
|» event_type|body|[WebhookV2Event](#schemawebhookv2event)|true|An enum representing the possible events that a webhook can subscribe to|
|» team_id|body|string|false|**Deprecated.** Team id to receive updates about. This is deprecated, use 'context' and 'context_id' instead.|
|» context|body|string|true|Context to create the webhook for. Must be "team", "project", or "file".|
|» context_id|body|string|true|The id of the context you want to receive updates about.|
|» endpoint|body|string|true|The HTTP endpoint that will receive a POST request when the event triggers. Max length 2048 characters.|
|» passcode|body|string|true|String that will be passed back to your webhook endpoint to verify that it is being called by Figma. Max length 100 characters.|
|» status|body|[WebhookV2Status](#schemawebhookv2status)|false|State of the webhook, including any error state it may be in|
|» description|body|string|false|User provided description or name for the webhook. Max length 150 characters.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» event_type|PING|
|» event_type|FILE_UPDATE|
|» event_type|FILE_VERSION_UPDATE|
|» event_type|FILE_DELETE|
|» event_type|LIBRARY_PUBLISH|
|» event_type|FILE_COMMENT|
|» event_type|DEV_MODE_STATUS_UPDATE|
|» status|ACTIVE|
|» status|PAUSED|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "event_type": "PING",
  "team_id": "string",
  "context": "string",
  "context_id": "string",
  "plan_api_id": "string",
  "status": "ACTIVE",
  "client_id": "string",
  "passcode": "string",
  "endpoint": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": true,
  "status": 400,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 403 Response

```json
{
  "status": 403,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "status": 500,
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h1 id="figma-api-activity-logs">Activity Logs</h1>

Get activity logs as an organization admin.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/activity-logs-endpoints/">Activity log endpoints documentation</a>

## Get activity logs

<a id="opIdgetActivityLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/activity_logs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/activity_logs`

Returns a list of activity log events

<h3 id="get-activity-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|events|query|string|false|Event type(s) to include in the response. Can have multiple values separated by comma. All events are returned by default.|
|start_time|query|number|false|Unix timestamp of the least recent event to include. This param defaults to one year ago if unspecified.|
|end_time|query|number|false|Unix timestamp of the most recent event to include. This param defaults to the current timestamp if unspecified.|
|limit|query|number|false|Maximum number of events to return. This param defaults to 1000 if unspecified.|
|order|query|string|false|Event order by timestamp. This param can be either "asc" (default) or "desc".|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|order|asc|
|order|desc|

```json
}
```

<h1 id="figma-api-developer-logs">Developer Logs</h1>

Get developer logs for REST API and MCP server requests in an organization.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/developer-logs-endpoints/">Developer log endpoints documentation</a>

## Get developer logs

<a id="opIdgetDeveloperLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/developer_logs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "token_type": "plan_access_token",
    "token": "string",
    "token_name": "string",
    "user_email": "string",
    "ip_address": "string",
    "event_source": "rest_api",
    "date_range": "last_30d",
    "limit": 25,
    "cursor": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /v1/developer_logs`

Returns a list of developer log entries for REST API and MCP server requests made within the organization. This endpoint requires a plan access token with the `org:developer_log_read` scope.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token_type": "plan_access_token",
  "token": "string",
  "token_name": "string",
  "user_email": "string",
  "ip_address": "string",
  "event_source": "rest_api",
  "date_range": "last_30d",
  "limit": 25,
  "cursor": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-developer-logs-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» token_type|body|string|false|Filter by the type of token used for authentication.|
|» token|body|string|false|Filter by token value(s). Multiple values can be separated by commas.|
|» token_name|body|string|false|Filter by token name prefix(es). Multiple values can be separated by commas.|
|» user_email|body|string|false|Filter by user email prefix(es). Multiple values can be separated by commas.|
|» ip_address|body|string|false|Filter by IP address prefix(es). Multiple values can be separated by commas.|
|» event_source|body|string|false|Filter by event source.|
|» date_range|body|string|false|Filter by date range.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|Maximum number of entries to return.|
|» cursor|body|string|false|A cursor returned from a previous request, used for pagination.|

#### Enumerated Values

|» token_type|plan_access_token|
|» token_type|developer_token|

|» event_source|rest_api|

|» date_range|last_7d|

<h1 id="figma-api-ai-usage">AI Usage</h1>

Get per-user, per-day AI credit usage for a plan.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/ai-usage-endpoints/">AI usage endpoints documentation</a>

## Get daily AI credit usage

<a id="opIdgetAiUsageDaily"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/ai_usage/daily?start_date=string&end_date=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/ai_usage/daily`

Returns per-user, per-day AI credit usage for the plan associated with the calling token. This endpoint requires a plan access token with the `org:ai_metering_usage_read` scope.

<h3 id="get-daily-ai-credit-usage-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start_date|query|string|true|The first day to include, inclusive, as a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date (UTC). Required. Must be on or after `2025-12-01` and no more than 366 days before the current UTC day.|
|end_date|query|string|true|The last day to include, inclusive, as a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date (UTC). Required. Must be on or after `start_date` and the current UTC day or earlier.|
|user_email|query|string|false|Restrict the results to a single Figma user, identified by email. When omitted, rows for every user in the plan with usage in the range are returned. An email that matches no Figma user returns a 400.|
|limit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of rows to return. This param defaults to 1000 if unspecified, and may not exceed 1000.|
|cursor|query|string|false|An opaque cursor returned from a previous request, used for pagination.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rows": [
    {
      "plan_id": "string",
      "user_id": "string",
      "user_email": "string",
      "day": "string",
      "editor_type": "design",
      "seat_credits_sum": 0,
      "plan_credits_sum": 0,
      "workspace_id": "string",
      "workspace_name": "string",
      "team_id": "string",
      "team_name": "string",
      "license_group_id": "string",
      "license_group_name": "string",
      "metering_period_start": "string",
      "metering_period_end": "string"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": "string",
  "has_next_page": true
}
```

```json
  "error": true,
  "status": 400,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
  "status": 401,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
}
```

<h1 id="figma-api-payments">Payments</h1>

Get purchase information for your Community resources.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/payments-endpoints/">Payment endpoints documentation</a>

## Get payments

<a id="opIdgetPayments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/payments \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/payments`

There are two methods to query for a user's payment information on a plugin, widget, or Community file. The first method, using plugin payment tokens, is typically used when making queries from a plugin's or widget's code. The second method, providing a user ID and resource ID, is typically used when making queries from anywhere else.

Note that you can only query for resources that you own. In most cases, this means that you can only query resources that you originally created.

<h3 id="get-payments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|plugin_payment_token|query|string|false|Short-lived token returned from "getPluginPaymentTokenAsync" in the plugin payments API and used to authenticate to this endpoint. Read more about generating this token through "Calling the Payments REST API from a plugin or widget" below.|
|user_id|query|string|false|The ID of the user to query payment information about. You can get the user ID by having the user OAuth2 to the Figma REST API.|
|community_file_id|query|string|false|The ID of the Community file to query a user's payment information on. You can get the Community file ID from the file's Community page (look for the number after "file/" in the URL). Provide exactly one of "community_file_id", "plugin_id", or "widget_id".|
|plugin_id|query|string|false|The ID of the plugin to query a user's payment information on. You can get the plugin ID from the plugin's manifest, or from the plugin's Community page (look for the number after "plugin/" in the URL). Provide exactly one of "community_file_id", "plugin_id", or "widget_id".|
|widget_id|query|string|false|The ID of the widget to query a user's payment information on. You can get the widget ID from the widget's manifest, or from the widget's Community page (look for the number after "widget/" in the URL). Provide exactly one of "community_file_id", "plugin_id", or "widget_id".|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "status": 200,
  "error": false,
  "meta": {
    "user_id": "string",
    "resource_id": "string",
    "resource_type": "PLUGIN",
    "payment_status": {
      "type": "UNPAID"
    },
    "date_of_purchase": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

```json
  "error": true,
  "status": 401,
  "message": "string"
}
```

```json
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json

  "error": true,
  "status": 500,
  "message": "string"
}
```

<h1 id="figma-api-variables">Variables</h1>

Interact with variables in an Enterprise organization.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/variables-endpoints/">Variables endpoints documentation</a>

## Get local variables

<a id="opIdgetLocalVariables"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/variables/local \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}/variables/local`

**This API is available to full members of Enterprise orgs.**

The `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/local` endpoint lets you enumerate local variables created in the file and remote variables used in the file. Remote variables are referenced by their `subscribed_id`.

As a part of the Variables related API additions, the `GET /v1/files/:file_key` endpoint now returns a `boundVariables` property, containing the `variableId` of the bound variable. The `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/local` endpoint can be used to get the full variable or variable collection object.

Note that `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/published` does not return modes. Instead, you will need to use the `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/local` endpoint, in the same file, to examine the mode values.
        

<h3 id="get-local-variables-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to get variables from. This can be a file key or branch key. Use `GET /v1/files/:key` with the `branch_data` query param to get the branch key.|

## Get published variables

<a id="opIdgetPublishedVariables"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/variables/published \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/files/{file_key}/variables/published`

**This API is available to full members of Enterprise orgs.**

The `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/published` endpoint returns the variables that are published from the given file.

The response for this endpoint contains some key differences compared to the `GET /v1/files/:file_key/variables/local` endpoint:

- Each variable and variable collection contains a `subscribed_id`.
- Modes are omitted for published variable collections

Published variables have two ids: an id that is assigned in the file where it is created (`id`), and an id that is used by subscribing files (`subscribed_id`). The `id` and `key` are stable over the lifetime of the variable. The `subscribed_id` changes every time the variable is modified and published. The same is true for variable collections.

The `updatedAt` fields are ISO 8601 timestamps that indicate the last time that a change to a variable was published. For variable collections, this timestamp will change any time a variable in the collection is changed.

<h3 id="get-published-variables-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File to get variables from. This must be a main file key, not a branch key, as it is not possible to publish from branches.|

## Create/modify/delete variables

<a id="opIdpostVariables"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/variables \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "variableCollections": [
      {
        "action": "CREATE",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "initialModeId": "string",
        "hiddenFromPublishing": false,
        "parentVariableCollectionId": "string",
        "initialModeIdToParentModeIdMapping": {
          "property1": "string",
          "property2": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "variableModes": [
      {
        "action": "CREATE",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "variableCollectionId": "string"
      }
    ],
    "variables": [
      {
        "action": "CREATE",
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "variableCollectionId": "string",
        "resolvedType": "BOOLEAN",
        "description": "string",
        "hiddenFromPublishing": false,
        "scopes": [
          "ALL_SCOPES"
        ],
        "codeSyntax": {
          "WEB": "string",
          "ANDROID": "string",
          "iOS": "string"
        }
      }
    ],
    "variableModeValues": [
      {
        "variableId": "string",
        "modeId": "string",
        "value": true
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/files/{file_key}/variables`

**This API is available to full members of Enterprise orgs with Editor seats.**

The `POST /v1/files/:file_key/variables` endpoint lets you bulk create, update, and delete variables and variable collections.

The request body supports the following 4 top-level arrays. Changes from these arrays will be applied in the below order, and within each array, by array order.

- **variableCollections**: For creating, updating, and deleting variable collections
- **variableModes**: For creating, updating, and deleting modes within variable collections
  - Each collection can have a maximum of 40 modes
  - Mode names cannot be longer than 40 characters
- **variables**: For creating, updating, and deleting variables
  - Each collection can have a maximum of 5000 variables
  - Variable names must be unique within a collection and cannot contain certain special characters such as `.{}`
- **variableModeValues**: For setting a variable value under a specific mode.
  - When setting aliases, a variable cannot be aliased to itself or form an alias cycle
  - Color variables can use a composed color value with `color` and `opacity` fields. At least one field must be a variable alias.

Temporary ids can be used to reference an object later in the same POST request body. They can be used at create time in the `id` property of variable collections, modes, variables, and in the `initialModeId` property of variable collections. They are scoped to a single request body, and must be unique within the body. The mapping of temporary ids to real ids is returned in the response.

This endpoint has the following key behaviors:

- The request body must be 4MB or less.
- Must include an `action` property for collections, modes, and variables to tell the API whether to create, update, or delete the object.
- When creating a collection, mode, or variable, you can include a temporary `id` that can be referenced in dependent objects in the same request. For example, you can create a new collection with the id `"my_new_collection"`. You can then set `variableCollectionId` to `"my_new_collection"` in new modes or variables. Temporary ids must be unique in the request body.
- New collections always come with one mode. You can reference this mode by setting `initialModeId` to a temporary id in the request body. This is useful if you want to set values for variables in the mode in the `variableModeValues` array.
  - The `tempIdToRealId` array returns a mapping of the temporary ids in the request, to the real ids of the newly created objects.
- When adding new modes or variables, default variable values will be applied, consistent with what happens in the UI.
- Everything to be created, updated, and deleted in the request body is treated as one atomic operation. If there is any validation failure, you will get a 400 status code response, and no changes will be persisted.
- You will not be able to update remote variables or variable collections. You can only update variables in the file where they were originally created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variableCollections": [
    {
      "action": "CREATE",
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "initialModeId": "string",
      "hiddenFromPublishing": false,
      "parentVariableCollectionId": "string",
      "initialModeIdToParentModeIdMapping": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "variableModes": [
    {
      "action": "CREATE",
```

## Update dev resources

<a id="opIdputDevResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/dev_resources \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dev_resources": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "name": "string",
        "url": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /v1/dev_resources`

Bulk update dev resources across multiple files.

Ids for dev resources that are successfully updated will show up in the `links_updated` array in the response.

If there are any dev resources that cannot be updated, you may still get a 200 response. These resources will show up in the `errors` array.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dev_resources": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "url": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|» » id|body|string|true|Unique identifier of the dev resource|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the dev resource.|
|» » url|body|string|false|The URL of the dev resource.|

## Create dev resources

<a id="opIdpostDevResources"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/dev_resources \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "dev_resources": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "url": "string",
        "file_key": "string",
        "node_id": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /v1/dev_resources`

Bulk create dev resources across multiple files.
Dev resources that are successfully created will show up in the links_created array in the response.

If there are any dev resources that cannot be created, you may still get a 200 response. These resources will show up in the errors array. Some reasons a dev resource cannot be created include:

- Resource points to a `file_key` that cannot be found.
- The node already has the maximum of 10 dev resources.
- Another dev resource for the node has the same url.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dev_resources": [
    {
      "name": "string",
      "url": "string",
      "file_key": "string",
      "node_id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-dev-resources-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|true|A list of dev resources that you want to create.|
|» dev_resources|body|[object]|true|An array of dev resources.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the dev resource.|
|» » url|body|string|true|The URL of the dev resource.|
|» » file_key|body|string|true|The file key where the dev resource belongs.|
|» » node_id|body|string|true|The target node to attach the dev resource to.|

## Delete dev resource

<a id="opIddeleteDevResource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.figma.com/v1/files/string/dev_resources/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`DELETE /v1/files/{file_key}/dev_resources/{dev_resource_id}`

Delete a dev resource from a file

<h3 id="delete-dev-resource-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|The file to delete the dev resource from. This must be a main file key, not a branch key.|
|dev_resource_id|path|string|true|The id of the dev resource to delete.|

> Example responses

> 401 Response

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/analytics/libraries/string/component/actions?group_by=component' \
```

`GET /v1/analytics/libraries/{file_key}/component/actions`

## Get library analytics variable action data.

<a id="opIdgetLibraryAnalyticsVariableActions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/analytics/libraries/string/variable/actions?group_by=variable' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/analytics/libraries/{file_key}/variable/actions`

Returns a list of library analytics variable actions data broken down by the requested dimension.

<h3 id="get-library-analytics-variable-action-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_key|path|string|true|File key of the library to fetch analytics data for.|
|cursor|query|string|false|Cursor indicating what page of data to fetch. Obtained from prior API call.|
|group_by|query|string|true|A dimension to group returned analytics data by.|
|start_date|query|string|false|ISO 8601 date string (YYYY-MM-DD) of the earliest week to include. Dates are rounded back to the nearest start of a week. Defaults to one year prior.|
|end_date|query|string|false|ISO 8601 date string (YYYY-MM-DD) of the latest week to include. Dates are rounded forward to the nearest end of a week. Defaults to the latest computed week.|

<h1 id="figma-api-oembed">oEmbed</h1>

Get oEmbed data for Figma files and published Makes.

<a href="https://developers.figma.com/docs/rest-api/oembed-endpoints/">oEmbed endpoint documentation</a>

## Get oEmbed data

<a id="opIdgetOEmbed"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://api.figma.com/v1/oembed?url=string' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "X-Figma-Token: ${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /v1/oembed`

Returns oEmbed data for a Figma file or published Make site URL, following the [oEmbed specification](https://oembed.com/).

<h3 id="get-oembed-data-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|url|query|string|true|The URL of the Figma file or published Make site to retrieve oEmbed data for.|
|maxwidth|query|integer|false|Maximum width of the embed in pixels. Defaults to 800. The response width will be adjusted to maintain a 16:9 aspect ratio with maxheight.|
|maxheight|query|integer|false|Maximum height of the embed in pixels. Defaults to 450. The response height will be adjusted to maintain a 16:9 aspect ratio with maxwidth.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "version": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "key": "string",
  "url": "string",
  "provider_name": "string",
  "provider_url": "string",
  "cache_age": 0,
  "width": 0,
  "height": 0,
  "html": "string",
  "is_published_site": true,
  "folder_name": "string",
  "thumbnail_url": "string",
  "thumbnail_width": 0,
  "thumbnail_height": 0
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": true,
  "status": 400,
  "message": "string"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "status": 404,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 429 Response

```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "err": "string"
}
```

> 501 Response

```json
{
  "status": 501,
  "err": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="get-oembed-data-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Response from the GET /v1/oembed endpoint.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad request. Parameters are invalid or malformed. Please check the input formats. This error can also happen if the requested resources are too large to complete the request, which results in a timeout. Please reduce the number and size of objects requested.|Inline|
|404|Not Found|The requested file or resource was not found.|Inline|
|429|Too Many Requests|In some cases API requests may be throttled or rate limited. Please wait a while before attempting the request again (typically a minute).|Inline|
|501|Not Implemented|The server does not support the functionality required to fulfill the request.|Inline|

<h3 id="get-oembed-data-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|string|true|none|The oEmbed specification version. Always "1.0".|
|type|string|true|none|The oEmbed response type. Always "rich".|
|title|string|true|none|The title of the Figma file or published Make site.|
|key|string|false|none|The key of the Figma file. Not present for published Makes|
|url|string|true|none|The canonical URL of the resource.|
|provider_name|string|true|none|The name of the content provider. Always "Figma" or "Make".|
|provider_url|string|true|none|The URL of the content provider's website. Always "https://www.figma.com".|
|cache_age|integer|true|none|Suggested cache lifetime for this response in seconds. Always 3600.|
|width|integer|true|none|Width of the embed in pixels.|
|height|integer|true|none|Height of the embed in pixels.|
|html|string|true|none|The HTML for embedding the file. Contains an iframe pointing to the Figma embed URL.|
|is_published_site|boolean|false|none|Only present and "true" when the resource is a published Make.|
|folder_name|string|false|none|The name of the folder containing the file, if the file resides in a folder.|
|thumbnail_url|string|false|none|URL of a thumbnail image for the file.|
|thumbnail_width|integer|false|none|Width of the thumbnail image in pixels.|
|thumbnail_height|integer|false|none|Height of the thumbnail image in pixels.|

Status Code **400**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|error|boolean|true|none|For erroneous requests, this value is always `true`.|
|status|number|true|none|Status code|
|message|string|true|none|A string describing the error|
|status|number|true|none|Status code|

|---|---|
|error|true|
|status|400|

|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|

```json
{
  "absoluteBoundingBox": {

    "width": 0,
    "height": 0
  },

  "constraints": {
    "vertical": "TOP",
    "horizontal": "LEFT"
  },
  "relativeTransform": [
    [
      0,
      0,
      0
    ],
    [
      0,
      0,
      0
    ]
  ],
  "size": {
    "x": 0,
    "y": 0
  },
  "layoutAlign": "INHERIT",
  "layoutGrow": 0,
  "layoutPositioning": "AUTO",
  "minWidth": 0,
  "maxWidth": 0,
  "minHeight": 0,
  "maxHeight": 0,
  "layoutSizingHorizontal": "FIXED",
  "layoutSizingVertical": "FIXED",
  "gridRowCount": 0,
  "gridColumnCount": 0,
  "gridRowGap": 0,
  "gridColumnGap": 0,
  "gridColumnsSizing": "string",
  "gridRowsSizing": "string",
  "gridChildHorizontalAlign": "AUTO",
  "gridChildVerticalAlign": "AUTO",
  "gridRowSpan": 1,
  "gridColumnSpan": 1,
  "gridRowAnchorIndex": 0,
  "gridColumnAnchorIndex": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|clipsContent|boolean|true|none|Whether or not this node clip content outside of its bounds|
|background|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Background of the node. This is deprecated, as backgrounds for frames are now in the `fills` field.|
|backgroundColor|[RGBA](#schemargba)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Background color of the node. This is deprecated, as frames now support more than a solid color as a background. Please use the `fills` field instead.|
|layoutGrids|[[LayoutGrid](#schemalayoutgrid)]|false|none|An array of layout grids attached to this node (see layout grids section for more details). GROUP nodes do not have this attribute|
|overflowDirection|string|false|none|Whether a node has primary axis scrolling, horizontal or vertical.|
|layoutMode|string|false|none|Whether this layer uses auto-layout to position its children.|
|primaryAxisSizingMode|string|false|none|Whether the primary axis has a fixed length (determined by the user) or an automatic length (determined by the layout engine). This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|counterAxisSizingMode|string|false|none|Whether the counter axis has a fixed length (determined by the user) or an automatic length (determined by the layout engine). This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|primaryAxisAlignItems|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame's children should be aligned in the primary axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|counterAxisAlignItems|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame's children should be aligned in the counter axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingLeft|number|false|none|The padding between the left border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingRight|number|false|none|The padding between the right border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingTop|number|false|none|The padding between the top border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingBottom|number|false|none|The padding between the bottom border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|itemSpacing|number|false|none|The distance between children of the frame. Can be negative. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|itemReverseZIndex|boolean|false|none|Determines the canvas stacking order of layers in this frame. When true, the first layer will be draw on top. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|strokesIncludedInLayout|boolean|false|none|Determines whether strokes are included in layout calculations. When true, auto-layout frames behave like css "box-sizing: border-box". This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|layoutWrap|string|false|none|Whether this auto-layout frame has wrapping enabled.|
|counterAxisSpacing|number|false|none|The distance between wrapped tracks of an auto-layout frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutWrap: "WRAP"`|
|counterAxisAlignContent|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame’s wrapped tracks should be aligned in the counter axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutWrap: "WRAP"`.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cornerRadius|number|false|none|Radius of each corner if a single radius is set for all corners|
|cornerSmoothing|number|false|none|A value that lets you control how "smooth" the corners are. Ranges from 0 to 1. 0 is the default and means that the corner is perfectly circular. A value of 0.6 means the corner matches the iOS 7 "squircle" icon shape. Other values produce various other curves.|
|rectangleCornerRadii|[number]|false|none|Array of length 4 of the radius of each corner of the frame, starting in the top left and proceeding clockwise.<br><br>Values are given in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.|

<h2 id="tocS_HasMaskTrait">HasMaskTrait</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemahasmasktrait"></a>
<a id="schema_HasMaskTrait"></a>
<a id="tocShasmasktrait"></a>
<a id="tocshasmasktrait"></a>

```json
{
  "isMask": false,
  "maskType": "ALPHA",
  "isMaskOutline": false
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|maskType|ALPHA|
|maskType|VECTOR|
|maskType|LUMINANCE|

|---|---|---|---|---|
|characters|string|true|none|The raw characters in the text node.|
