|characterStyleOverrides|[number]|true|none|The array corresponds to characters in the text box, where each element references the 'styleOverrideTable' to apply specific styles to each character. The array's length can be less than or equal to the number of characters due to the removal of trailing zeros. Elements with a value of 0 indicate characters that use the default type style. If the array is shorter than the total number of characters, the characters beyond the array's length also use the default style.|
|layoutVersion|number|false|none|Internal property, preserved for backward compatibility. Avoid using this value.|
|styleOverrideTable|object|true|none|Map from ID to TypeStyle for looking up style overrides.|
|lineTypes|[string]|true|none|An array with the same number of elements as lines in the text node, where lines are delimited by newline or paragraph separator characters. Each element in the array corresponds to the list type of a specific line. List types are represented as string enums with one of these possible values:<br><br>- `NONE`: Not a list item.<br>- `ORDERED`: Text is an ordered list (numbered).<br>- `UNORDERED`: Text is an unordered list (bulleted).|
|lineIndentations|[number]|true|none|An array with the same number of elements as lines in the text node, where lines are delimited by newline or paragraph separator characters. Each element in the array corresponds to the indentation level of a specific line.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|lineTypes|NONE|
|lineTypes|ORDERED|
|lineTypes|UNORDERED|


### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|characters|string|true|none|The raw characters in the text path node.|
|style|[TextPathTypeStyle](#schematextpathtypestyle)|true|none|Style of text including font family and weight.|
|characterStyleOverrides|[number]|true|none|The array corresponds to characters in the text box, where each element references the 'styleOverrideTable' to apply specific styles to each character. The array's length can be less than or equal to the number of characters due to the removal of trailing zeros. Elements with a value of 0 indicate characters that use the default type style. If the array is shorter than the total number of characters, the characters beyond the array's length also use the default style.|
|layoutVersion|number|false|none|Internal property, preserved for backward compatibility. Avoid using this value.|
|styleOverrideTable|object|true|none|Map from ID to TextPathTypeStyle for looking up style overrides.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|
|blendMode|[BlendMode](#schemablendmode)|true|none|How this node blends with nodes behind it in the scene (see blend mode section for more details)|
|opacity|number|false|none|Opacity of the node|
|children|[[SubcanvasNode](#schemasubcanvasnode)]|true|none|An array of nodes that are direct children of this node|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|clipsContent|boolean|true|none|Whether or not this node clip content outside of its bounds|
|background|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|**Deprecated.** Background of the node. This is deprecated, as backgrounds for frames are now in the `fills` field.|
|backgroundColor|[RGBA](#schemargba)|false|none|**Deprecated.** Background color of the node. This is deprecated, as frames now support more than a solid color as a background. Please use the `fills` field instead.|
|layoutGrids|[[LayoutGrid](#schemalayoutgrid)]|false|none|An array of layout grids attached to this node (see layout grids section for more details). GROUP nodes do not have this attribute|
|overflowDirection|string|false|none|Whether a node has primary axis scrolling, horizontal or vertical.|
|layoutMode|string|false|none|Whether this layer uses auto-layout to position its children.|
|primaryAxisSizingMode|string|false|none|Whether the primary axis has a fixed length (determined by the user) or an automatic length (determined by the layout engine). This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|counterAxisSizingMode|string|false|none|Whether the counter axis has a fixed length (determined by the user) or an automatic length (determined by the layout engine). This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|primaryAxisAlignItems|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame's children should be aligned in the primary axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|counterAxisAlignItems|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame's children should be aligned in the counter axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingLeft|number|false|none|The padding between the left border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingRight|number|false|none|The padding between the right border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingTop|number|false|none|The padding between the top border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|paddingBottom|number|false|none|The padding between the bottom border of the frame and its children. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|itemSpacing|number|false|none|The distance between children of the frame. Can be negative. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|itemReverseZIndex|boolean|false|none|Determines the canvas stacking order of layers in this frame. When true, the first layer will be draw on top. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|strokesIncludedInLayout|boolean|false|none|Determines whether strokes are included in layout calculations. When true, auto-layout frames behave like css "box-sizing: border-box". This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames.|
|layoutWrap|string|false|none|Whether this auto-layout frame has wrapping enabled.|
|counterAxisSpacing|number|false|none|The distance between wrapped tracks of an auto-layout frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutWrap: "WRAP"`|
|counterAxisAlignContent|string|false|none|Determines how the auto-layout frame’s wrapped tracks should be aligned in the counter axis direction. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutWrap: "WRAP"`.|
|cornerRadius|number|false|none|Radius of each corner if a single radius is set for all corners|
|cornerSmoothing|number|false|none|A value that lets you control how "smooth" the corners are. Ranges from 0 to 1. 0 is the default and means that the corner is perfectly circular. A value of 0.6 means the corner matches the iOS 7 "squircle" icon shape. Other values produce various other curves.|
|rectangleCornerRadii|[number]|false|none|Array of length 4 of the radius of each corner of the frame, starting in the top left and proceeding clockwise.<br><br>Values are given in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.|
|fills|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|true|none|An array of fill paints applied to the node.|
|styles|object|false|none|A mapping of a StyleType to style ID (see Style) of styles present on this node. The style ID can be used to look up more information about the style in the top-level styles field.|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|
|fillOverrideTable|object|false|none|Map from ID to PaintOverride for looking up fill overrides. To see which regions are overridden, you must use the `geometry=paths` option. Each path returned may have an `overrideID` which maps to this table.|
|fillGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object fill.|
|strokeGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object stroke.|
|strokeCap|string|false|none|A string enum describing the end caps of vector paths.|
|strokeMiterAngle|number|false|none|Only valid if `strokeJoin` is "MITER". The corner angle, in degrees, below which `strokeJoin` will be set to "BEVEL" to avoid super sharp corners. By default this is 28.96 degrees.|
|exportSettings|[[ExportSetting](#schemaexportsetting)]|false|none|An array of export settings representing images to export from the node.|
|effects|[[Effect](#schemaeffect)]|true|none|An array of effects attached to this node (see effects section for more details)|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|
|transitionNodeID|string|false|none|Node ID of node to transition to in prototyping|
|transitionDuration|number|false|none|The duration of the prototyping transition on this node (in milliseconds). This will override the default transition duration on the prototype, for this node.|
|transitionEasing|[EasingType](#schemaeasingtype)|false|none|The easing curve used in the prototyping transition on this node.|
|interactions|[[Interaction](#schemainteraction)]|false|none|none|
|individualStrokeWeights|[StrokeWeights](#schemastrokeweights)|false|none|An object including the top, bottom, left, and right stroke weights. Only returned if individual stroke weights are used.|
|devStatus|object|false|none|Represents whether or not a node has a particular handoff (or dev) status applied to it.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|
|blendMode|[BlendMode](#schemablendmode)|true|none|How this node blends with nodes behind it in the scene (see blend mode section for more details)|
|opacity|number|false|none|Opacity of the node|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|fills|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|true|none|An array of fill paints applied to the node.|
|styles|object|false|none|A mapping of a StyleType to style ID (see Style) of styles present on this node. The style ID can be used to look up more information about the style in the top-level styles field.|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|
|fillOverrideTable|object|false|none|Map from ID to PaintOverride for looking up fill overrides. To see which regions are overridden, you must use the `geometry=paths` option. Each path returned may have an `overrideID` which maps to this table.|
|fillGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object fill.|
|strokeGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object stroke.|
|strokeCap|string|false|none|A string enum describing the end caps of vector paths.|
|strokeMiterAngle|number|false|none|Only valid if `strokeJoin` is "MITER". The corner angle, in degrees, below which `strokeJoin` will be set to "BEVEL" to avoid super sharp corners. By default this is 28.96 degrees.|
|exportSettings|[[ExportSetting](#schemaexportsetting)]|false|none|An array of export settings representing images to export from the node.|
|effects|[[Effect](#schemaeffect)]|true|none|An array of effects attached to this node (see effects section for more details)|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|
|transitionNodeID|string|false|none|Node ID of node to transition to in prototyping|
|transitionDuration|number|false|none|The duration of the prototyping transition on this node (in milliseconds). This will override the default transition duration on the prototype, for this node.|
|transitionEasing|[EasingType](#schemaeasingtype)|false|none|The easing curve used in the prototyping transition on this node.|
|interactions|[[Interaction](#schemainteraction)]|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|
|blendMode|[BlendMode](#schemablendmode)|true|none|How this node blends with nodes behind it in the scene (see blend mode section for more details)|
|opacity|number|false|none|Opacity of the node|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|fills|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|true|none|An array of fill paints applied to the node.|
|styles|object|false|none|A mapping of a StyleType to style ID (see Style) of styles present on this node. The style ID can be used to look up more information about the style in the top-level styles field.|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|
|fillOverrideTable|object|false|none|Map from ID to PaintOverride for looking up fill overrides. To see which regions are overridden, you must use the `geometry=paths` option. Each path returned may have an `overrideID` which maps to this table.|
|fillGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object fill.|
|strokeGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object stroke.|
|strokeCap|string|false|none|A string enum describing the end caps of vector paths.|
|strokeMiterAngle|number|false|none|Only valid if `strokeJoin` is "MITER". The corner angle, in degrees, below which `strokeJoin` will be set to "BEVEL" to avoid super sharp corners. By default this is 28.96 degrees.|
|exportSettings|[[ExportSetting](#schemaexportsetting)]|false|none|An array of export settings representing images to export from the node.|
|effects|[[Effect](#schemaeffect)]|true|none|An array of effects attached to this node (see effects section for more details)|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|
|transitionNodeID|string|false|none|Node ID of node to transition to in prototyping|
|transitionDuration|number|false|none|The duration of the prototyping transition on this node (in milliseconds). This will override the default transition duration on the prototype, for this node.|
|transitionEasing|[EasingType](#schemaeasingtype)|false|none|The easing curve used in the prototyping transition on this node.|
|interactions|[[Interaction](#schemainteraction)]|false|none|none|
|cornerRadius|number|false|none|Radius of each corner if a single radius is set for all corners|
|cornerSmoothing|number|false|none|A value that lets you control how "smooth" the corners are. Ranges from 0 to 1. 0 is the default and means that the corner is perfectly circular. A value of 0.6 means the corner matches the iOS 7 "squircle" icon shape. Other values produce various other curves.|
|rectangleCornerRadii|[number]|false|none|Array of length 4 of the radius of each corner of the frame, starting in the top left and proceeding clockwise.<br><br>Values are given in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|
|blendMode|[BlendMode](#schemablendmode)|true|none|How this node blends with nodes behind it in the scene (see blend mode section for more details)|
|opacity|number|false|none|Opacity of the node|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|fills|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|true|none|An array of fill paints applied to the node.|
|styles|object|false|none|A mapping of a StyleType to style ID (see Style) of styles present on this node. The style ID can be used to look up more information about the style in the top-level styles field.|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|
|fillOverrideTable|object|false|none|Map from ID to PaintOverride for looking up fill overrides. To see which regions are overridden, you must use the `geometry=paths` option. Each path returned may have an `overrideID` which maps to this table.|
|fillGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object fill.|
|strokeGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object stroke.|
|strokeCap|string|false|none|A string enum describing the end caps of vector paths.|
|strokeMiterAngle|number|false|none|Only valid if `strokeJoin` is "MITER". The corner angle, in degrees, below which `strokeJoin` will be set to "BEVEL" to avoid super sharp corners. By default this is 28.96 degrees.|
|exportSettings|[[ExportSetting](#schemaexportsetting)]|false|none|An array of export settings representing images to export from the node.|
|effects|[[Effect](#schemaeffect)]|true|none|An array of effects attached to this node (see effects section for more details)|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|
|transitionNodeID|string|false|none|Node ID of node to transition to in prototyping|
|transitionDuration|number|false|none|The duration of the prototyping transition on this node (in milliseconds). This will override the default transition duration on the prototype, for this node.|
|transitionEasing|[EasingType](#schemaeasingtype)|false|none|The easing curve used in the prototyping transition on this node.|
|interactions|[[Interaction](#schemainteraction)]|false|none|none|
|cornerRadius|number|false|none|Radius of each corner if a single radius is set for all corners|
|cornerSmoothing|number|false|none|A value that lets you control how "smooth" the corners are. Ranges from 0 to 1. 0 is the default and means that the corner is perfectly circular. A value of 0.6 means the corner matches the iOS 7 "squircle" icon shape. Other values produce various other curves.|
|rectangleCornerRadii|[number]|false|none|Array of length 4 of the radius of each corner of the frame, starting in the top left and proceeding clockwise.<br><br>Values are given in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left.|
|individualStrokeWeights|[StrokeWeights](#schemastrokeweights)|false|none|An object including the top, bottom, left, and right stroke weights. Only returned if individual stroke weights are used.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|children|[[CanvasNode](#schemacanvasnode)]|true|none|none|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|DOCUMENT|
|scrollBehavior|SCROLLS|
|scrollBehavior|FIXED|
|scrollBehavior|STICKY_SCROLLS|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|The type of this node, represented by the string literal "BOOLEAN_OPERATION"|
|booleanOperation|string|true|none|A string enum indicating the type of boolean operation applied.|
|id|string|true|none|A string uniquely identifying this node within the document.|
|name|string|true|none|The name given to the node by the user in the tool.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the node|
|visible|boolean|false|none|Whether or not the node is visible on the canvas.|
|locked|boolean|false|none|If true, layer is locked and cannot be edited|
|isFixed|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** Whether the layer is fixed while the parent is scrolling|
|scrollBehavior|string|true|none|How layer should be treated when the frame is resized|
|rotation|number|false|none|The rotation of the node, if not 0.|
|componentPropertyReferences|object|false|none|A mapping of a layer's property to component property name of component properties attached to this node. The component property name can be used to look up more information on the corresponding component's or component set's componentPropertyDefinitions.|
|pluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible only to the plugin that wrote it. Requires the `pluginData` to include the ID of the plugin.|
|sharedPluginData|object|false|none|Data written by plugins that is visible to all plugins. Requires the `pluginData` parameter to include the string "shared".|
|boundVariables|object|false|none|A mapping of field to the variables applied to this field. Most fields will only map to a single `VariableAlias`. However, for properties like `fills`, `strokes`, `size`, `componentProperties`, and `textRangeFills`, it is possible to have multiple variables bound to the field.|
|explicitVariableModes|object|false|none|A mapping of variable collection ID to mode ID representing the explicitly set modes for this node.|
|blendMode|[BlendMode](#schemablendmode)|true|none|How this node blends with nodes behind it in the scene (see blend mode section for more details)|
|opacity|number|false|none|Opacity of the node|
|children|[[SubcanvasNode](#schemasubcanvasnode)]|true|none|An array of nodes that are direct children of this node|
|absoluteBoundingBox|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|Bounding box of the node in absolute space coordinates.|
|absoluteRenderBounds|[Rectangle](#schemarectangle) \| null|true|none|The actual bounds of a node accounting for drop shadows, thick strokes, and anything else that may fall outside the node's regular bounding box defined in `x`, `y`, `width`, and `height`. The `x` and `y` inside this property represent the absolute position of the node on the page. This value will be `null` if the node is invisible.|
|preserveRatio|boolean|false|none|Keep height and width constrained to same ratio.|
|constraints|[LayoutConstraint](#schemalayoutconstraint)|false|none|Horizontal and vertical layout constraints for node.|
|relativeTransform|[Transform](#schematransform)|false|none|The top two rows of a matrix that represents the 2D transform of this node relative to its parent. The bottom row of the matrix is implicitly always (0, 0, 1). Use to transform coordinates in geometry. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|fills|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|true|none|An array of fill paints applied to the node.|
|styles|object|false|none|A mapping of a StyleType to style ID (see Style) of styles present on this node. The style ID can be used to look up more information about the style in the top-level styles field.|
|strokes|[[Paint](#schemapaint)]|false|none|An array of stroke paints applied to the node.|
|strokeWeight|number|false|none|The weight of strokes on the node.|
|strokeAlign|string|false|none|Position of stroke relative to vector outline, as a string enum<br><br>- `INSIDE`: stroke drawn inside the shape boundary<br>- `OUTSIDE`: stroke drawn outside the shape boundary<br>- `CENTER`: stroke drawn centered along the shape boundary|
|strokeJoin|string|false|none|A string enum with value of "MITER", "BEVEL", or "ROUND", describing how corners in vector paths are rendered.|
|strokeDashes|[number]|false|none|An array of floating point numbers describing the pattern of dash length and gap lengths that the vector stroke will use when drawn.<br><br>For example a value of [1, 2] indicates that the stroke will be drawn with a dash of length 1 followed by a gap of length 2, repeated.|
|fillOverrideTable|object|false|none|Map from ID to PaintOverride for looking up fill overrides. To see which regions are overridden, you must use the `geometry=paths` option. Each path returned may have an `overrideID` which maps to this table.|
|fillGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object fill.|
|strokeGeometry|[[Path](#schemapath)]|false|none|Only specified if parameter `geometry=paths` is used. An array of paths representing the object stroke.|
|strokeCap|string|false|none|A string enum describing the end caps of vector paths.|
|strokeMiterAngle|number|false|none|Only valid if `strokeJoin` is "MITER". The corner angle, in degrees, below which `strokeJoin` will be set to "BEVEL" to avoid super sharp corners. By default this is 28.96 degrees.|
|exportSettings|[[ExportSetting](#schemaexportsetting)]|false|none|An array of export settings representing images to export from the node.|
|effects|[[Effect](#schemaeffect)]|true|none|An array of effects attached to this node (see effects section for more details)|
|isMask|boolean|false|none|Does this node mask sibling nodes in front of it?|
|maskType|string|false|none|If this layer is a mask, this property describes the operation used to mask the layer's siblings. The value may be one of the following:<br><br>- ALPHA: the mask node's alpha channel will be used to determine the opacity of each pixel in the masked result.<br>- VECTOR: if the mask node has visible fill paints, every pixel inside the node's fill regions will be fully visible in the masked result. If the mask has visible stroke paints, every pixel inside the node's stroke regions will be fully visible in the masked result.<br>- LUMINANCE: the luminance value of each pixel of the mask node will be used to determine the opacity of that pixel in the masked result.|
|isMaskOutline|boolean|false|none|**Deprecated.** True if maskType is VECTOR. This field is deprecated; use maskType instead.|
|transitionNodeID|string|false|none|Node ID of node to transition to in prototyping|
|transitionDuration|number|false|none|The duration of the prototyping transition on this node (in milliseconds). This will override the default transition duration on the prototype, for this node.|
|transitionEasing|[EasingType](#schemaeasingtype)|false|none|The easing curve used in the prototyping transition on this node.|
|interactions|[[Interaction](#schemainteraction)]|false|none|none|

|size|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Width and height of element. This is different from the width and height of the bounding box in that the absolute bounding box represents the element after scaling and rotation. Only present if `geometry=paths` is passed.|
|layoutAlign|string|false|none|<br>Determines if the layer should stretch along the parent's counter axis. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `INHERIT`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In previous versions of auto layout, determined how the layer is aligned inside an auto-layout frame. This property is only provided for direct children of auto-layout frames.<br><br>- `MIN`<br>- `CENTER`<br>- `MAX`<br>- `STRETCH`<br><br>In horizontal auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "TOP" and "BOTTOM". In vertical auto-layout frames, "MIN" and "MAX" correspond to "LEFT" and "RIGHT".|
|layoutGrow|number|false|none|This property is applicable only for direct children of auto-layout frames, ignored otherwise. Determines whether a layer should stretch along the parent's primary axis. A `0` corresponds to a fixed size and `1` corresponds to stretch.|
|layoutPositioning|string|false|none|Determines whether a layer's size and position should be determined by auto-layout settings or manually adjustable.|
|minWidth|number|false|none|The minimum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxWidth|number|false|none|The maximum width of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|minHeight|number|false|none|The minimum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|maxHeight|number|false|none|The maximum height of the frame. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames or direct children of auto-layout frames.|
|layoutSizingHorizontal|string|false|none|The horizontal sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|layoutSizingVertical|string|false|none|The vertical sizing setting on this auto-layout frame or frame child.<br>- `FIXED`<br>- `HUG`: only valid on auto-layout frames and text nodes<br>- `FILL`: only valid on auto-layout frame children|
|gridRowCount|number|false|none|The number of rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnCount|number|false|none|The number of columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowGap|number|false|none|The distance between rows in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnGap|number|false|none|The distance between columns in the grid layout. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-columns property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowsSizing|string|false|none|The string for the CSS grid-template-rows property. This property is only applicable for auto-layout frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildHorizontalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the horizontal direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridChildVerticalAlign|string|false|none|Determines how a GRID frame's child should be aligned in the vertical direction within its grid area. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowSpan|number|false|none|The number of rows that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnSpan|number|false|none|The number of columns that a GRID frame's child should span. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridRowAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the row that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|gridColumnAnchorIndex|number|false|none|The index of the column that a GRID frame's child should be anchored to. This property is only applicable for direct children of frames with `layoutMode: "GRID"`.|
|devStatus|object|false|none|Represents whether or not a node has a particular handoff (or dev) status applied to it.|
