<h2 id="tocS_Trigger">Trigger</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematrigger"></a>
<a id="schema_Trigger"></a>
<a id="tocStrigger"></a>
<a id="tocstrigger"></a>

```json
{
  "type": "ON_CLICK"
}
```

The `"ON_HOVER"` and `"ON_PRESS"` trigger types revert the navigation when the trigger is finished (the result is temporary). 
`"MOUSE_ENTER"`, `"MOUSE_LEAVE"`, `"MOUSE_UP"` and `"MOUSE_DOWN"` are permanent, one-way navigation.
The `delay` parameter requires the trigger to be held for a certain duration of time before the action occurs.
Both `timeout` and `delay` values are in milliseconds.
The `"ON_MEDIA_HIT"` and `"ON_MEDIA_END"` trigger types can only trigger from a video. 
They fire when a video reaches a certain time or ends. The `timestamp` value is in seconds.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[AfterTimeoutTrigger](#schemaaftertimeouttrigger)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|delay|number|true|none|none|
|deprecatedVersion|boolean|false|none|Whether this is a [deprecated version](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/360040035834-Prototype-triggers#h_01HHN04REHJNP168R26P1CMP0A) of the trigger that was left unchanged for backwards compatibility.<br>If not present, the trigger is the latest version.|
|*oneOf*|[OnKeyDownTrigger](#schemaonkeydowntrigger)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|[OnMediaHitTrigger](#schemaonmediahittrigger)|false|none|none|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|none|
|type|string|true|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|ON_CLICK|
|type|ON_HOVER|
|type|ON_PRESS|
|type|ON_DRAG|
|type|MOUSE_ENTER|
|type|MOUSE_LEAVE|
|type|MOUSE_UP|
|type|MOUSE_DOWN|
|type|ON_MEDIA_END|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|true|none|none|
|destinationId|string \| null|true|none|none|
|navigation|[Navigation](#schemanavigation)|true|none|The method of navigation. The possible values are:<br>- `"NAVIGATE"`: Replaces the current screen with the destination, also closing all overlays.<br>- `"OVERLAY"`: Opens the destination as an overlay on the current screen.<br>- `"SWAP"`: On an overlay, replaces the current (topmost) overlay with the destination. On a top-level frame, <br>  behaves the same as `"NAVIGATE"` except that no entry is added to the navigation history.<br>- `"SCROLL_TO"`: Scrolls to the destination on the current screen.<br>- `"CHANGE_TO"`: Changes the closest ancestor instance of source node to the specified variant.|
|transition|[Transition](#schematransition) \| null|true|none|none|
|preserveScrollPosition|boolean|false|none|Whether the scroll offsets of any scrollable elements in the current screen or overlay are preserved when navigating to the destination. This is applicable only if the layout of both the current frame and its destination are the same.|
|overlayRelativePosition|[Vector](#schemavector)|false|none|Applicable only when `navigation` is `"OVERLAY"` and the destination is a frame with `overlayPosition` equal to `"MANUAL"`. This value represents the offset by which the overlay is opened relative to this node.|
|resetVideoPosition|boolean|false|none|When true, all videos within the destination frame will reset their memorized playback position to 00:00 before starting to play.|
|resetScrollPosition|boolean|false|none|Whether the scroll offsets of any scrollable elements in the current screen or overlay reset when navigating to the destination. This is applicable only if the layout of both the current frame and its destination are the same.|
|resetInteractiveComponents|boolean|false|none|Whether the state of any interactive components in the current screen or overlay reset when navigating to the destination. This is applicable if there are interactive components in the destination frame.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|type|NODE|
|navigation|NAVIGATE|
|navigation|SWAP|
|navigation|OVERLAY|
|navigation|SCROLL_TO|
|navigation|CHANGE_TO|

<h2 id="tocS_Navigation">Navigation</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemanavigation"></a>
<a id="schema_Navigation"></a>
<a id="tocSnavigation"></a>
<a id="tocsnavigation"></a>

```json
"NAVIGATE"
```

The method of navigation. The possible values are:
- `"NAVIGATE"`: Replaces the current screen with the destination, also closing all overlays.
- `"OVERLAY"`: Opens the destination as an overlay on the current screen.
- `"SWAP"`: On an overlay, replaces the current (topmost) overlay with the destination. On a top-level frame, 
  behaves the same as `"NAVIGATE"` except that no entry is added to the navigation history.
- `"SCROLL_TO"`: Scrolls to the destination on the current screen.
- `"CHANGE_TO"`: Changes the closest ancestor instance of source node to the specified variant.

<h2 id="tocS_VariableScope">VariableScope</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemavariablescope"></a>
<a id="schema_VariableScope"></a>
<a id="tocSvariablescope"></a>
<a id="tocsvariablescope"></a>

```json
"ALL_SCOPES"
```

Scopes allow a variable to be shown or hidden in the variable picker for various fields. This declutters the Figma UI if you have a large number of variables. Variable scopes are currently supported on `FLOAT`, `STRING`, and `COLOR` variables.

`ALL_SCOPES` is a special scope that means that the variable will be shown in the variable picker for all variable fields. If `ALL_SCOPES` is set, no additional scopes can be set.

`ALL_FILLS` is a special scope that means that the variable will be shown in the variable picker for all fill fields. If `ALL_FILLS` is set, no additional fill scopes can be set.

Valid scopes for `FLOAT` variables:
- `ALL_SCOPES`
- `TEXT_CONTENT`
- `WIDTH_HEIGHT`
- `GAP`
- `STROKE_FLOAT`
- `EFFECT_FLOAT`
- `OPACITY`
- `COLOR_OPACITY`
- `FONT_WEIGHT`
- `FONT_SIZE`
- `LINE_HEIGHT`
- `LETTER_SPACING`
- `PARAGRAPH_SPACING`
- `PARAGRAPH_INDENT`

`OPACITY` corresponds to layer opacity, while `COLOR_OPACITY` corresponds to the opacity channel of a color.

Valid scopes for `STRING` variables:
- `ALL_SCOPES`
- `TEXT_CONTENT`
- `FONT_FAMILY`
- `FONT_STYLE`

Valid scopes for `COLOR` variables:
- `ALL_SCOPES`
- `ALL_FILLS`
- `FRAME_FILL`
- `SHAPE_FILL`
- `TEXT_FILL`
- `STROKE_COLOR`
- `EFFECT_COLOR`

A grouping of related Variable objects each with the same modes.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of this variable collection.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of this variable collection.|
|key|string|true|none|The key of this variable collection.|
|modes|[object]|true|none|The modes of this variable collection.|
|defaultModeId|string|true|none|The id of the default mode.|
|remote|boolean|true|none|Whether this variable collection is remote.|
|isExtension|boolean|false|none|Whether this variable collection is an extension of another variable collection.|
|parentVariableCollectionId|string|false|none|The id of the parent variable collection that this variable collection is an extension of. If this variable collection is not an extension, this value will be `undefined`.|
|rootVariableCollectionId|string|false|none|The id of the root variable collection in the extension chain. This is the ID of the original (non-extended) collection at the top of the parent chain. For example, if Collection C extends B which extends A (root), then `rootVariableCollectionId` is A's ID. If this variable collection is not an extension, this value will be `undefined`.|
|variableOverrides|object|false|none|The overrides for the variables in this variable collection as a map of variable ids to a map of mode ids to variable values.|
|hiddenFromPublishing|boolean|true|none|Whether this variable collection is hidden when publishing the current file as a library.|
|variableIds|[string]|true|none|The ids of the variables in the collection. Note that the order of these variables is roughly the same as what is shown in Figma Design, however it does not account for groups. As a result, the order of these variables may not exactly reflect the exact ordering and grouping shown in the authoring UI.|

  },

}

A Variable is a single design token that defines values for each of the modes in its VariableCollection. These values can be applied to various kinds of design properties.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The unique identifier of this variable.|
|name|string|true|none|The name of this variable.|
|key|string|true|none|The key of this variable.|
|variableCollectionId|string|true|none|The id of the variable collection that contains this variable.|
|resolvedType|[VariableResolvedDataType](#schemavariableresolveddatatype)|true|none|The resolved type of the variable.|
|valuesByMode|object|true|none|The values for each mode of this variable.|
|remote|boolean|true|none|Whether this variable is remote.|
|description|string|true|none|The description of this variable.|
|hiddenFromPublishing|boolean|true|none|Whether this variable is hidden when publishing the current file as a library.<br><br>If the parent `VariableCollection` is marked as `hiddenFromPublishing`, then this variable will also be hidden from publishing via the UI. `hiddenFromPublishing` is independently toggled for a variable and collection. However, both must be true for a given variable to be publishable.|
|scopes|[[VariableScope](#schemavariablescope)]|true|none|An array of scopes in the UI where this variable is shown. Setting this property will show/hide this variable in the variable picker UI for different fields.<br><br>Setting scopes for a variable does not prevent that variable from being bound in other scopes (for example, via the Plugin API). This only limits the variables that are shown in pickers within the Figma UI.|
|codeSyntax|[VariableCodeSyntax](#schemavariablecodesyntax)|true|none|An object containing platform-specific code syntax definitions for a variable. All platforms are optional.|
|deletedButReferenced|boolean|false|none|Indicates that the variable was deleted in the editor, but the document may still contain references to the variable. References to the variable may exist through bound values or variable aliases.|
